# Experiment Design — Effect of `period` on PDF Model Performance on ETTm1

> **Submission contract.** Design-only document. Not executed in this workspace. The sandbox contains only `/workspace/task.json`; no source code, no dataset files, no `track.md`, no `torch`/`numpy`/`pandas`, no GPU, no network. All commitments below are by explicit researcher direction and are reproduced verbatim in the Assumptions & Threats register so reviewers can audit the claim scope.

---

## 1. Objective & Research Question

**Question.** *How do different period settings affect the performance of the PDF model on the ETTm1 dataset?*

**Objective.** Quantify how the period hyperparameter `P` entered into the PDF model influences forecasting quality on ETTm1, and characterize the answer as a function of the forecast horizon.

**Primary endpoint.** Test-set MSE and MAE on the normalized ETTm1 test split, aggregated across 5 seeds, for each cell of the (period × horizon) grid.

**Secondary endpoints.** Paired statistical comparison between adjacent period levels (Wilcoxon, FDR-corrected); sanity-check from a "P = lookback" ablation; absolute anchor from a non-PDF baseline.

---

## 2. Assumptions Register

These **are assumptions, not facts from a repository**. The repository contains no PDF source, no ETTm1 data, and no `track.md`; the only artifact at `/workspace` is the `task.json` shown to the researcher. Each item reproduces a binding commitment from the researcher.

| ID | Commitment | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **A1** | `PDF` is interpreted as the period-/frequency-aware block from the **PatchTST family** of models — the interpretation most consistent with the de facto use of "PDF" in ETTm1-style benchmark literature. The protocol is conditional on this interpretation. If the actual implementation is a different paper, only the *motivation* of the period grid would shift; the design logic would not. | Researcher direction |
| **A2** | `period` is a **single scalar** `P` per training run. The design does **not** depend on period-lists, multi-period inputs, or learned periods. A multi-period variant is mentioned only as a bracketed follow-up in the Discussion, not as part of the main cell matrix. | Researcher direction |
| **A3** | Model hyperparameters are **inherited from the canonical ETTm1 default config and are not re-tuned per period**. This is by design: re-tuning per `P` would confound the effect we are measuring. | Researcher direction |
| **A4** | Only one **canonical ETTm1 train/val/test split** is used (Zhou et al., 2021: train ≈ first 12 months, val ≈ next 4 months, test ≈ final 4 months, in raw rows). No re-splitting, no sliding-window cross-validation as a substitute. | Researcher direction + Reference |
| **A5** | "Performance" = **MSE and MAE evaluated in normalized space** (StandardScaler fit on train only, applied to val and test), consistent with how PatchTST-family tables report ETTm1 numbers. | Researcher direction |

---

## 3. Fixed Factors

All factors below are held constant across every cell of the design. Changing any of them invalidates the comparison; if such a change is later found necessary, it is treated as an out-of-scope perturbation and must be re-run on all cells.

### 3.1 Data & split

- **Dataset.** ETTm1 (`ETTm1.csv`), 15-minute granularity, 7 channels (oil temperature + 6 power-load features).
- **Loading.** Read from a local copy of the canonical ETTm1 file. No resampling, no imputation beyond what the source file already provides (which is none — the series is gap-free).
- **Split.** Fixed canonical split (Zhou et al., 2021, Informer release): `train = rows[0 : 12·30·96)`, `val = rows[12·30·96 : 16·30·96)`, `test = rows[16·30·96 : 20·30·96)`. Numbers are exact and identical across all cells.
- **Normalization.** `StandardScaler.fit(train)` → apply to train/val/test. Scaler never rebuilt.

### 3.2 Preprocessing & windowing

- **Lookback** `L = 96` (1 day of 15-min samples). Held constant across all cells.
- **Sliding windows** constructed inside each split independently; no window crosses a split boundary.
- **Horizons** reported, four canonical values: `H ∈ {96, 192, 336, 720}`.
- **Channel handling.** All channels used; no target-only restricted setting.

### 3.3 Model hyperparameters

- **Architecture.** PDF block (PatchTST-family period-/frequency-aware block), exact layer widths/numbers, attention heads, dropout, patch length, and stride **taken verbatim from the canonical ETTm1 default config** for this model family. Recorded in a frozen `config_ettm1.yaml` and not edited per cell.
- **`period` `P`** is the **only** non-fixed model input. All other architectural knobs come from the same frozen config.

### 3.4 Optimizer, scheduler, early stopping

- **Optimizer.** AdamW.
- **Learning rate.** One fixed value (e.g. `1e-3`), identical across all cells.
- **Scheduler.** Cosine schedule, identical across all cells.
- **Batch size.** One fixed value taken from the ETTm1 default config; identical across all cells.
- **Early stopping.** **Required**, identical across all cells:
  - `max_epochs = 100`
  - `patience = 10` on **val MSE**
  - `restore_best_weights = True`
- **Best-checkpoint definition.** Val MSE at end of epoch, computed on the entire val split, no early-stopping on val MAE.

### 3.5 Seeds

- Five seeds for the primary analysis: `seeds ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}`.
- Each seed controls Python, NumPy, and PyTorch RNGs and the model-init RNG; data shuffling (if any) is seeded; dataloader workers are seeded.
- Seeds are reported per-cell in every output table.

### 3.6 Metrics

- **Primary.** `MSE` and `MAE` on the **normalized** test split, computed once per cell `(P, H, seed)` and aggregated.
- **Secondary (informational, optional).** MSE/MAE in the original (un-normalized) scale for sanity checks only; not used for the headline conclusion.
- **Aggregation.** Per cell, report `mean`, `std`, and a **95 % bootstrap confidence interval** (resampling with replacement, `N = 1000`, seed = cell seed for reproducibility) over the 5 seed-level MSE/MAE values.

---

## 4. Independent Variable & Grid

**Independent variable:** scalar `P ∈ ℕ⁺`, the period passed to the PDF block.

**Primary grid (used for all headline cells):**

| `P` | Interpretation (at 15-min granularity) |
|---|---|
| `24`  | 6 hours — sub-daily |
| `48`  | 12 hours — sub-daily |
| `96`  | 1 day (24 h) — daily cycle |
| `168` | weekly cycle, expressed in **hours**; in points = `168 × 4 = 672`. *Correction during implementation:* this value is the **hour** form. The points-form mapping for the period is `P_points = 168 × 4 = 672`. To stay consistent with the grid as written in points, treat `168` as **"weekly" expressed as the hour-value**, and use the **points equivalent** in code; the cells are reported under both labels in the final table with a one-line clarification, or the **points form** `672` is used directly and described as the weekly cycle in 15-min steps. Same logic applies to `336` = 2 weeks = `336 × 4 = 1344` points and `672` = monthly (≈ 28 days) = `672 × 4 = 2688` points. |
| `336` | 2-week cycle (in hours); points form = `1344`. |
| `672` | monthly / 4-week cycle (in hours); points form = `2688`. |

> **Binding clarification.** The five researcher-supplied values `{24, 48, 96, 168, 336, 672}` are in the paper's *hour* convention for the larger values, while the smaller values are sub-daily in *hours*. To remove ambiguity inside the implementation report, the design commits to using the **points form** at 15-min granularity as the actual values of `P` passed to the model: `P_points ∈ {24, 48, 96, 672·4=original-168-as-points, 336·4=1344, 672·4=2688}` — re-stated as label-value pairs in Section 8 and a footnote in the final table. The grid topology (6 levels, 3 sub-daily, 3 ≥ weekly) is unchanged.

**Cell matrix (primary, full factorial):**

```
cells_primary = |P_grid| × |H_grid| × |seeds|
              = 6 × 4 × 5
              = 120 cells
```

**Exploratory tail (separate subsection, NOT merged into primary analysis):**

A second grid `{12, 16, 32, 64, 192, 384}` (sub-daily at finer resolutions, plus 2-day `192` and 4-day `384`) is reported in its own subsection labelled *Exploratory tail (not part of primary conclusion)*. Same protocols; results are **flagged as secondary** and excluded from the headline `period × horizon` table and from any rank-based inference.

---

## 5. Controls

Three controls. All run under identical (fixed) hyperparameters, seeds, and split.

1. **P = lookback ablation.** Repeat the entire grid with `P = L = 96` (and a separate run with `P = L ≫ H`, e.g. `P = 1536`, if `H = 720` is the largest horizon). Purpose: verify that the `period` knob has detectable leverage — i.e., that deviating from `P = lookback` changes MSE in a measurable direction. Without this control, a null result is uninterpretable.
2. **Non-PDF baseline.** Run at least one baseline per horizon × seed on the same split:
   - **Naive seasonal baseline** with `season = 96` (1-day repetition).
   - **Linear / DLinear** — taken from the released codebase and applied with its canonical ETTm1 config, fixed.
   - Purpose: anchor the absolute scale of MSE/MAE so that the `period → MSE` curves are read against a meaningful reference, and not just relatively.
3. **Fixed-canonic-split control.** Reported in the analysis as Section 6 row "Split integrity": the split file SHA-256 is recorded once at run start and asserted unchanged across all cells. No per-period or per-horizon re-splitting is permitted.

---

## 6. Analysis & Reporting Plan

### 6.1 Outputs

1. **`P × H` table (primary).** Rows = `P ∈ {24, 48, 96, 168, 336, 672}` (points form, see §4 clarification), columns = `H ∈ {96, 192, 336, 720}`, cells = `mean ± std` of normalized test MSE/MAE across `seeds ∈ {0,1,2,3,4}`. Each cell also carries the 95 % bootstrap CI (N=1000).
2. **`P × H` table (controls).** A second table reports (i) the `P = lookback` ablation rows and (ii) the non-PDF baselines (naive seasonal and DLinear) for the same H column set. Rows are clearly labelled so they cannot be confused with primary cells.
3. **Figure A — trend curves.** One panel per horizon. x-axis = `P` (linear or log, depending on span, with categorical tick labels preserving the table ordering), y-axis = normalized test MSE, error bars = ± std across seeds; smooth line connects cell means. Matching panels for MAE in supplementary material.
4. **Figure B — horizon interaction.** Heatmap of `mean(MSE)` indexed by `P × H`, with overlaid Δ-to-best text per row. Documents the fact (if present) that the relative ordering of `P` changes with `H`.
5. **Ranks (supplementary, secondary).** For each `H`, ranks of `P` by mean MSE; Wilcoxon signed-rank between adjacent `P` levels over the seed-matched pairs, FDR-corrected (Benjamini–Hochberg) across the comparisons in this horizon. **Explicitly labelled exploratory; not the primary claim.**
6. **Cell-level raw outputs.** A machine-readable `results.csv` with columns `(P, H, seed, MSE_norm, MAE_norm, MSE_orig, MAE_orig, best_epoch, total_epochs)`. One row per primary cell, plus rows for controls and exploratory tail.

### 6.2 Tie-breaking & "best period"

- "Best `P` for horizon `H`" is the `P` with the **lowest mean** normalized MSE, ties broken by lower mean MAE, then by lower std.
- No "best period overall" is reported unless horizons agree on it; disagreement across horizons is itself an output.

### 6.3 What counts as answer to the research question

- Whether the trend in `P → MSE` is monotone or non-monotone, per horizon.
- Whether the optimal `P` is horizon-dependent (§6.1, Figure B).
- The magnitude of the effect, expressed as MSE range (`max − min`) per horizon relative to the non-PDF baseline gap.

---

## 7. Threats to Validity

Reproduced from researcher direction and surfaced here as a register so reviewers can audit scope.

- **(a) Hyperparameter inheritance.** Hyperparameters (architecture widths, heads, dropout, patch length, stride, optimizer settings, scheduler, batch size, early-stopping policy) are **inherited from the ETTm1 default config and not re-tuned per `P`**. This is *by design* — re-tuning would confound the effect. The cost is that the absolute minimum of MSE over `P` may be higher than a tuned run could achieve; the claim being made is about **`P`-dependence under shared hyperparameters**, not about the global optimum.
- **(b) Dataset and unit.** Results are **specific to ETTm1 and 15-minute granularity**. The weekly and monthly labels in the grid therefore refer to **points, not hours** (and this is restated at the top of the final table; see §4 clarification). Transfer to ETTm2, ECL, weather, or hourly-granularity datasets is not assumed.
- **(c) Confidence-interval scope.** Reported CIs (and any std/FDR comparisons) are over **seed-to-seed variance only**. They do **not** cover variance from alternative splits, alternative preprocessing (e.g. RobustScaler vs StandardScaler), alternative windowing strategies, or alternative hyperparameter choices. Generalization across those axes is out of scope.

Additional threats worth noting (not in the researcher's three but unavoidable):

- **Lookback fixed at 96.** The interaction `P × L` is not probed. If the chosen `L` happens to be near-optimal for the daily cycle, this can mask an interaction.
- **No learning curve.** Differences in convergence speed across `P` are *allowed* to express themselves because early stopping is the same policy everywhere, but a per-cell training-curve plot is recommended as a sanity check (does any cell fail to converge?).
- **PDF interpretation.** If the actual PDF model is not the PatchTST-family block assumed in A1, the relative ordering of `P` values can shift but the methodological skeleton of the design (fixed everything else, vary `P`, multi-horizon, multi-seed, conservative aggregation) does not.

---

## 8. Feasibility & Compute Note

- **Design-only.** This document is the deliverable. The experiment is **not** executed in this workspace.
- **Sandbox constraints observed (design still produced).** The bubblewrap sandbox used here contains: only `/workspace/task.json`; no source repositories, no ETTm1 file, no `track.md`; Python 3.12 with no `torch`/`numpy`/`pandas` installed; GPU disabled; network disabled; 24 CPU cores available. These constraints do not prevent writing the design.
- **If executed outside the sandbox.** Expected to run in standard PyTorch on a single GPU (e.g. one consumer-class GPU). With `max_epochs = 100`, `patience = 10`, primary grid `|P|=6`, `|H|=4`, `|seeds|=5` → **120 cells** of primary experiments, plus **`~20` control cells** for `P = lookback` ablations and **`~40` baseline cells** (naive + DLinear × 4 horizons × 5 seeds). Indicative order: a few GPU-hours on a single modern GPU; CPU-only would multiply this by a large factor and is not recommended. The exploratory-tail grid in §4 adds `6 × 4 × 5 = 120` cells and is **optional**.

---

## 9. References & Provenance

- **ETTm1 dataset and canonical split.** Zhou, H., Zhang, S., Peng, J., Zhang, S., Li, J., Xiong, H., & Zhang, W. (2021). *Informer: Beyond Efficient Transformer for Long Sequence Time-Series Forecasting.* Proceedings of AAAI 2021. The 12-/4-/4-month train/val/test split on ETTm1 (in raw rows) is the de facto standard used by Informer, Autoformer, FEDformer, PatchTST, and adjacent benchmarks. The split values in §3.1 follow that convention.
- **Period-/frequency-aware block (PDF interpretation used here).** The model is assumed to be the period-aware block from the PatchTST family: Nie, Y., Nguyen, N. H., Sinthong, P., & Kalagnanam, J. (2023). *A Time Series is Worth 64 Words: Long-term Forecasting with Transformers.* ICLR 2023. If the intended `PDF` is a different paper (e.g. a probabilistic-density-forecast model, a different frequency-domain method, or a paper named "PDF" that this design has not anticipated), **only the motivation of `P` values in §4 would shift**; the design logic (fixed everything else, vary `P`, multi-horizon, multi-seed, conservative aggregation, controls, threats) would not.
- **Repository provenance (negative).** `/workspace` contains only `task.json` (389 B). No `track.md` is present despite reference in `documents`. No source code or dataset shipped. No claims about implementation details are made from the local repository.

---

## Assumptions & Threats Register (consolidated, audit-friendly)

This restates the §2 and §7 items in one block so a reviewer can read the entire claim scope without jumping.

**Assumptions (binding):**
- **A1.** PDF = period-/frequency-aware block from the PatchTST family. Protocol is conditional on this. If the actual implementation differs, only the motivation of the period grid shifts; design logic does not.
- **A2.** `period` is a single scalar `P` per training run. No period-lists, no learned periods in the main matrix.
- **A3.** Model hyperparameters are inherited from the canonical ETTm1 default config and **not** re-tuned per period.
- **A4.** One fixed canonical ETTm1 split (Zhou et al., 2021: 12/4/4 months in raw rows); no re-splitting.
- **A5.** MSE / MAE in normalized space; scaler fit on train only.

**Threats (enumerated):**
- **(a) HP inheritance.** Optimizer / scheduler / early-stopping / architecture knobs from the default ETTm1 config, identical across cells, not re-tuned per `P` — by design.
- **(b) Dataset / granularity specificity.** Statements are specific to ETTm1 at 15-minute granularity; weekly/monthly labels in the table are in **points**, not hours.
- **(c) CI scope.** 95 % bootstrap CIs and std/FDR comparisons are over seed-to-seed variance only; not over split / preprocessing / windowing / hyperparameter alternatives.

**Sandbox integrity (factual, not an assumption):** workspace contains only `/workspace/task.json`; `track.md` referenced in `task.json` is absent; Python 3.12 present, `torch`/`numpy`/`pandas` absent; GPU disabled; network disabled; CPU 24; document is design-only and the experiment was not run here.

- **Базовый набор** (рекомендую как первоочередной): `period ∈ {24, 48, 96, 168, 336, 672}`.

  - 336 — двухнедельный.
  - 672 — месячный (4-недельный) — позволяет проверить, что происходит при заведомо «длинном» периоде, который плохо покрывается короткими train-окнами.
- **Расширенный набор** (если бюджет позволяет): добавить `12, 16, 32, 64, 192, 384` для более плотной развёртки в окрестности суточного цикла и кратных ему.

**Что фиксируется во всех прогонах:**
- **Lookback** и **horizon** — зафиксировать один стандарт, например `lookback = 96`, `horizon ∈ {96, 192, 336, 720}` (классические для ETTm1) или хотя бы `horizon = 96` для основного прогона и отдельный прогон с `horizon = 336` как sanity check.

## 3. Fixed Factors

All factors below are held constant across every cell of the design. Changing any of them invalidates the comparison; if such a change is later found necessary, it is treated as an out-of-scope perturbation and must be re-run on all cells.

### 3.1 Data & split

- **Dataset.** ETTm1 (`ETTm1.csv`), 15-minute granularity, 7 channels (oil temperature + 6 power-load features).
- **Loading.** Read from a local copy of the canonical ETTm1 file. No resampling, no imputation beyond what the source file already provides (which is none — the series is gap-free).
- **Split.** Fixed canonical split (Zhou et al., 2021, Informer release): `train = rows[0 : 12·30·96)`, `val = rows[12·30·96 : 16·30·96)`, `test = rows[16·30·96 : 20·30·96)`. Numbers are exact and identical across all cells.
- **Normalization.** `StandardScaler.fit(train)` → apply to train/val/test. Scaler never rebuilt.

### 3.2 Preprocessing & windowing

- **Lookback** `L = 96` (1 day of 15-min samples). Held constant across all cells.
- **Sliding windows** constructed inside each split independently; no window crosses a split boundary.
- **Horizons** reported, four canonical values: `H ∈ {96, 192, 336, 720}`.
- **Channel handling.** All channels used; no target-only restricted setting.

### 3.3 Model hyperparameters

- **Architecture.** PDF block (PatchTST-family period-/frequency-aware block), exact layer widths/numbers, attention heads, dropout, patch length, and stride **taken verbatim from the canonical ETTm1 default config** for this model family. Recorded in a frozen `config_ettm1.yaml` and not edited per cell.
- **`period` `P`** is the **only** non-fixed model input. All other architectural knobs come from the same frozen config.

### 3.4 Optimizer, scheduler, early stopping

- **Optimizer.** AdamW.
- **Learning rate.** One fixed value (e.g. `1e-3`), identical across all cells.
- **Scheduler.** Cosine schedule, identical across all cells.
- **Batch size.** One fixed value taken from the ETTm1 default config; identical across all cells.
- **Early stopping.** **Required**, identical across all cells:
  - `max_epochs = 100`
  - `patience = 10` on **val MSE**
  - `restore_best_weights = True`
- **Best-checkpoint definition.** Val MSE at end of epoch, computed on the entire val split, no early-stopping on val MAE.

### 3.5 Seeds

- Five seeds for the primary analysis: `seeds ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}`.
- Each seed controls Python, NumPy, and PyTorch RNGs and the model-init RNG; data shuffling (if any) is seeded; dataloader workers are seeded.
- Seeds are reported per-cell in every output table.

### 3.6 Metrics

- **Primary.** `MSE` and `MAE` on the **normalized** test split, computed once per cell `(P, H, seed)` and aggregated.
- **Secondary (informational, optional).** MSE/MAE in the original (un-normalized) scale for sanity checks only; not used for the headline conclusion.
- **Aggregation.** Per cell, report `mean`, `std`, and a **95 % bootstrap confidence interval** (resampling with replacement, `N = 1000`, seed = cell seed for reproducibility) over the 5 seed-level MSE/MAE values.

## 5. Controls

Three controls. All run under identical (fixed) hyperparameters, seeds, and split.

1. **P = lookback ablation.** Repeat the entire grid with `P = L = 96` (and a separate run with `P = L ≫ H`, e.g. `P = 1536`, if `H = 720` is the largest horizon). Purpose: verify that the `period` knob has detectable leverage — i.e., that deviating from `P = lookback` changes MSE in a measurable direction. Without this control, a null result is uninterpretable.
2. **Non-PDF baseline.** Run at least one baseline per horizon × seed on the same split:
   - **Naive seasonal baseline** with `season = 96` (1-day repetition).
   - **Linear / DLinear** — taken from the released codebase and applied with its canonical ETTm1 config, fixed.
   - Purpose: anchor the absolute scale of MSE/MAE so that the `period → MSE` curves are read against a meaningful reference, and not just relatively.
3. **Fixed-canonic-split control.** Reported in the analysis as Section 6 row "Split integrity": the split file SHA-256 is recorded once at run start and asserted unchanged across all cells. No per-period or per-horizon re-splitting is permitted.

## 6. Analysis & Reporting Plan

### 6.1 Outputs

1. **`P × H` table (primary).** Rows = `P ∈ {24, 48, 96, 168, 336, 672}` (points form, see §4 clarification), columns = `H ∈ {96, 192, 336, 720}`, cells = `mean ± std` of normalized test MSE/MAE across `seeds ∈ {0,1,2,3,4}`. Each cell also carries the 95 % bootstrap CI (N=1000).
2. **`P × H` table (controls).** A second table reports (i) the `P = lookback` ablation rows and (ii) the non-PDF baselines (naive seasonal and DLinear) for the same H column set. Rows are clearly labelled so they cannot be confused with primary cells.
3. **Figure A — trend curves.** One panel per horizon. x-axis = `P` (linear or log, depending on span, with categorical tick labels preserving the table ordering), y-axis = normalized test MSE, error bars = ± std across seeds; smooth line connects cell means. Matching panels for MAE in supplementary material.
4. **Figure B — horizon interaction.** Heatmap of `mean(MSE)` indexed by `P × H`, with overlaid Δ-to-best text per row. Documents the fact (if present) that the relative ordering of `P` changes with `H`.
5. **Ranks (supplementary, secondary).** For each `H`, ranks of `P` by mean MSE; Wilcoxon signed-rank between adjacent `P` levels over the seed-matched pairs, FDR-corrected (Benjamini–Hochberg) across the comparisons in this horizon. **Explicitly labelled exploratory; not the primary claim.**
6. **Cell-level raw outputs.** A machine-readable `results.csv` with columns `(P, H, seed, MSE_norm, MAE_norm, MSE_orig, MAE_orig, best_epoch, total_epochs)`. One row per primary cell, plus rows for controls and exploratory tail.

### 6.2 Tie-breaking & "best period"

- "Best `P` for horizon `H`" is the `P` with the **lowest mean** normalized MSE, ties broken by lower mean MAE, then by lower std.
- No "best period overall" is reported unless horizons agree on it; disagreement across horizons is itself an output.

### 6.3 What counts as answer to the research question

- Whether the trend in `P → MSE` is monotone or non-monotone, per horizon.
- Whether the optimal `P` is horizon-dependent (§6.1, Figure B).
- The magnitude of the effect, expressed as MSE range (`max − min`) per horizon relative to the non-PDF baseline gap.

## 7. Threats to Validity

Reproduced from researcher direction and surfaced here as a register so reviewers can audit scope.

- **(a) Hyperparameter inheritance.** Hyperparameters (architecture widths, heads, dropout, patch length, stride, optimizer settings, scheduler, batch size, early-stopping policy) are **inherited from the ETTm1 default config and not re-tuned per `P`**. This is *by design* — re-tuning would confound the effect. The cost is that the absolute minimum of MSE over `P` may be higher than a tuned run could achieve; the claim being made is about **`P`-dependence under shared hyperparameters**, not about the global optimum.
- **(b) Dataset and unit.** Results are **specific to ETTm1 and 15-minute granularity**. The weekly and monthly labels in the grid therefore refer to **points, not hours** (and this is restated at the top of the final table; see §4 clarification). Transfer to ETTm2, ECL, weather, or hourly-granularity datasets is not assumed.
- **(c) Confidence-interval scope.** Reported CIs (and any std/FDR comparisons) are over **seed-to-seed variance only**. They do **not** cover variance from alternative splits, alternative preprocessing (e.g. RobustScaler vs StandardScaler), alternative windowing strategies, or alternative hyperparameter choices. Generalization across those axes is out of scope.

Additional threats worth noting (not in the researcher's three but unavoidable):

- **Lookback fixed at 96.** The interaction `P × L` is not probed. If the chosen `L` happens to be near-optimal for the daily cycle, this can mask an interaction.
- **No learning curve.** Differences in convergence speed across `P` are *allowed* to express themselves because early stopping is the same policy everywhere, but a per-cell training-curve plot is recommended as a sanity check (does any cell fail to converge?).
- **PDF interpretation.** If the actual PDF model is not the PatchTST-family block assumed in A1, the relative ordering of `P` values can shift but the methodological skeleton of the design (fixed everything else, vary `P`, multi-horizon, multi-seed, conservative aggregation) does not.
